existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 Bundle has hard local breaking changes, mostly from new invariants and required terminology. Top concerns are populating fullUrl, adding searchset self links, normalizing transaction/batch/history entries, updating link relation handling, and defining R6-to-R4 policy for Bundle.issues and subscription notifications.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should validate against Bundle root constraints, not just element cardinality. Update generators and enums for link relation and Bundle.type changes. Treat Bundle.issues and subscription-notification as forward-only R6 features unless an explicit R4 mapping is defined.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition and local terminology deltas because both packages and indexes were available. Confidence is lower for prevalence and prose-only enforcement because no official diff, live terminology expansion, rendered narrative, or instance corpus was used.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
Bundle keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 5 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 2 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 7 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is normative/FMM 5, which creates strong stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 84/100, producing migration shape `moderate-targeted-remodel`, major migration `Partial`, and compatibility posture `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`.

10 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Expect targeted migration work, but continue reviewing individual breaks. Because R4 stability pressure is strong, low-cost compatible designs should be preferred unless they clearly undermine the R6 goal.

topFindings.title: Bundle.link.relation changes from string to code with a required IANA binding
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 Bundles with relation strings outside the packaged IANA value set can become invalid; runtime/API/codegen: SDKs may also change from free string handling to code or enum validation.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 enforces Bundle.entry.fullUrl for most non-batch/non-transaction entries
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: structurally accepted R4 instances without fullUrl can become R6 validation failures for non-exempt Bundle types, although many such instances were already questionable against R4 prose.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
